chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Dawud al-Raqqi, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "It is written in the Torah: Kafalah (guarantee), Nidamah (suretyship/companionship), Garamah (liability/compensation)."

key_terms.اَلتَّوْرَاةِ: The Torah; the holy book of the Israelites, cited here as a source for legal concepts.
key_terms.غَرَامَةٌ: Liability, compensation, or fine; refers to the financial responsibility or debt incurred.
key_terms.كَفَالَةٌ: Guarantee or suretyship; a legal contract where one party guarantees the debt or obligation of another.
key_terms.نَدَامَةٌ: Suretyship or companionship; often used in legal contexts to refer to the guarantor or the act of guaranteeing.

ai.seo_question: What are the three terms for guarantee and suretyship mentioned in the Torah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the pre-Islamic validity of financial suretyship (*Kafalah*) by citing its roots in the Torah, a common motif in Shia jurisprudence to demonstrate continuity with previous divine laws. The triad of terms—*Kafalah* (guarantee), *Nidamah* (often interpreted as the guarantor or the act of assuming responsibility), and *Garamah* (liability/compensation)—provides the foundational lexicon for Islamic contract law regarding debt and damages.
